## demo_database.items
# Model: `items`

Order line items. One row per unit sold (no quantity column): units = row count. Join to orders for dates/stores and to products for name, type and price. For any sales-by-product, product-mix or category-share question, use the line_sales measure here. Do NOT use products.price:sum from this model: it sums each distinct product's price once, not once per item sold.

source_model.name: supply_usage
source_model.sql: select s.name as supply_name, s.cost as cost from items i join orders o on i.order_id = o.id join supplies s on s.sku = i.sku where o.ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' and o.ordered_at < '2026-01-01'

args.message: Coffee cost the most of any supply component in 2025: $97,151.08 in total. To get this, I took every item sold in 2025 (each item row is one unit), matched it to that product's supply rows, added up the unit costs and grouped them by supply name. Grouping by name means a component used in several products counts as one. Costs are stored in cents, so I divided by 100. Chai mix was second at $91,092.96.
